name: folder-head-drag-reorders-folders
description: A folder head can be picked up and dragged among its siblings. The drag is synthesised as real dragstart/dragover/drop DOM events with a DataTransfer against the real running sidebar, the same events installRowDrag listens for. The head's own [data-dropzone] is the group-into-folder target for a TAB, so the scenario also proves that a FOLDER dragged over another folder's head resolves to the shared folders list (the drop indicator line, not that head's own highlight) rather than being refused as an attempt to group a folder into a folder.

actions.expression: (() => { const heads = [...document.querySelectorAll('.folderlist > .frow[data-folder-id]')]; return heads.length === 2 && heads.every(h => h.draggable === true) ? 'both draggable' : 'not both draggable: ' + heads.map(h => h.draggable).join(','); })()

(() => { const heads = [...document.querySelectorAll('.folderlist > .frow[data-folder-id]')]; const news = heads.find(h => h.dataset.folderId === '11111111-7477-4774-8774-747747747747'); const sports = heads.find(h => h.dataset.folderId === '22222222-7477-4774-8774-747747747747'); if (!news || !sports) { return 'missing-heads'; } const dt = new DataTransfer(); news.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragstart', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt})); const rect = sports.getBoundingClientRect(); const clientY = rect.top + rect.height * 0.75; sports.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragover', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt, clientX: rect.left + 5, clientY})); const line = document.querySelector('.dropline'); const shown = !!line && line.hidden === false; sports.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('drop', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt, clientX: rect.left + 5, clientY})); return 'dragged News onto Sports lower half, indicator ' + (shown ? 'shown' : 'NOT shown'); })()
actions.note: Hovering Sports's OWN head while dragging a folder must redirect to the shared folders zone (the targetFor fix) or the drop is refused as a group-into-folder attempt and the line never shows.
Read AFTER the drop, so it is the snapshot the native handler wrote back through atrium_core_reorder_folder - not the DOM the drag left behind.

Cmd+Q and start again against the same staged file, the way relaunch-file-readback does it. Cmd+Q rather than a kill, because the shutdown save in PostMainMessageLoopRun is part of the write path this question is about.
Read from a document the relaunch built, so it is the persisted order rather than anything the drag left in memory.

assertions.desc: News before Sports, the fixture's groups order

assertions.expected: "dragged News onto Sports lower half, indicator shown"

assertions.desc: Sports before News after the drop, read back from the snapshot the native handler persisted
The reordered folders survive a real quit and relaunch
